candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the bytes of the HAProxy v2 PROXY header. After the fixed 16-byte header and address block, each TLV is attacker-defined: type byte 0x20 (PP2_TYPE_SSL), 2-byte length, then a 1-byte client bit field, 4-byte verify value, and additional nested TLVs. Repeating this structure creates unbounded recursion depth while keeping total size within the decoder's normal maximum header size.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The decoder bounds the total v2 header size (V1_MAX_LENGTH/V2_MAX_LENGTH and configurable maxTlvSize), so the finding is not an unbounded-size allocation from a single length field. However, the size bound does not bound recursion depth. The decoder does catch HAProxyProtocolException around decodeHeader, but StackOverflowError and IndexOutOfBoundsException are not caught by that block. I did not execute or fuzz the parser, so the exact stack depth reached in a given deployment remains unverified.
candidates.impact: Remote denial of service: deep recursion exhausts the thread stack and raises StackOverflowError rather than a caught protocol exception, potentially disrupting the event-loop connection handling. In addition, malformed SSL TLV lengths can trigger unchecked IndexOutOfBoundsException paths in the same parsing code, so the decoder is not robust against hostile proxy headers.
candidates.prerequisites: The application pipeline must install HAProxyMessageDecoder and be reachable by the attacker (typical when Netty is deployed behind an HAProxy-compatible load balancer). No authentication is required. The crafted v2 header must be accepted by findVersion/findEndOfHeader and its total length must stay within v2MaxHeaderSize (roughly 16 + 65535 bytes); a nested SSL TLV frame can be as small as roughly 9 bytes, so roughly thousands of recursive frames fit.
candidates.root_cause: HAProxyMessage.readNextTLV handles a PP2_TYPE_SSL TLV by decoding its encapsulated TLVs in a loop that calls readNextTLV again. Because nested SSL TLVs are accepted recursively and no nesting-depth or recursion limit is enforced, an attacker can build a deeply nested TLV chain. The enclosing v2 header is bounded by v2MaxHeaderSize (about 65 KB) but that still permits thousands of recursive frames.
candidates.title: Unbounded recursion in HAProxyMessage.readNextTLV allows remote StackOverflowError
candidates.trace: HAProxyMessageDecoder.decode() -> HAProxyMessage.decodeHeader(ByteBuf) -> readTlvs(header) (line 243) -> readNextTLV(header) (line 260). When type is PP2_TYPE_SSL, readNextTLV reads the SSL payload and, if at least 4 bytes remain, loops calling readNextTLV on the inner ByteBuf (line 282). If that inner TLV is again PP2_TYPE_SSL, the same branch recurses. The call stack depth is therefore controlled by the attacker's nesting, and no depth counter is present in this path.
candidates.unverified: No runtime execution, compiler run, or fuzzing was performed. The exact stack size/depth needed to trigger StackOverflowError and the behavior of the surrounding Netty pipeline on Error propagation were not runtime-verified. The nested-TLV wire format was reconstructed from the source and HAProxy v2 TLV structure.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-674 Uncontrolled Recursion / CWE-400 Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

coverage_summary: Examined the assigned 2,115-file source scope. Reviewed codec/handler paths for HTTP/1.x and HTTP/2, HAProxy, DNS, MQTT, Redis, SPDY, SOCKS, compression/codec parsing, TLS/SslHandler/SNI, multipart HTTP decoding, buffer and common utilities. No test sources were present in the snapshot, and no code execution, build, scanner, or exploit run was performed.
limitations: No runtime confirmation: all findings are source-review leads, not reproduced vulnerabilities.
The snapshot contains no src/test tree, so upstream regression/security tests could not be inspected.
Exploitability depends on the application pipeline and on how untrusted inputs reach each decoder; those integration details are outside this source snapshot.
Large native modules and some codec/handler files were reviewed selectively rather than line-by-line, so other vulnerabilities may remain uninspected.
The exact upstream revision and CVE association are inferred from source/version content, not from git metadata or external advisories.

rejected_leads.lead: SslClientHelloHandler allocates ctx.alloc().buffer(handshakeLength) from a 24-bit ClientHello length before the full handshake is received (handler/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/ssl/SslClientHelloHandler.java:117-142).
rejected_leads.reason: This is a credible remote OOM/amplification issue, but it depends on SniHandler/SslClientHelloHandler being deployed and on the attacker being able to make the handler allocate the declared length; I could not tie it to a specific fix in this snapshot and it is less directly evidenced than the HAProxy recursion path.

rejected_leads.lead: HttpPostRequestDecoder / HttpPostMultipartRequestDecoder accumulate undecodedChunk and multipart fields without an enforced total-size or field-count limit (codec-http/.../multipart/HttpPost*.java).
rejected_leads.reason: Potentially serious DoS, but default factory MAXSIZE is unlimited by design and exploitability depends on application integration and configuration; the code paths are diffuse and not as self-contained as the recursion candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: DefaultHttpHeaders header-name/value validation permits invalid token characters such as control bytes and several separators (codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/DefaultHttpHeaders.java:368-415,444-513), and HttpObjectDecoder normalizes some trailing whitespace.
rejected_leads.reason: This could enable smuggling against normalization-mismatched intermediaries, but it requires an assumption about intermediary behavior and is better classified as a hardening/validation gap than a source-confirmed vulnerability in this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: HTTP/1.0 multiple Content-Length handling and TE+CL parsing are lenient in HttpObjectDecoder/HttpUtil.
rejected_leads.reason: The code deliberately handles duplicates differently for HTTP/1.0 and TE+CL only removes Content-Length for HTTP/1.1; exploitation depends on an intermediary with conflicting framing behavior, so it remained an unconfirmed smuggling lead.

rejected_leads.lead: NativeLibraryLoader writes and loads a native library from a temporary path (common/src/main/java/io/netty/util/internal/NativeLibraryLoader.java:170-196).
rejected_leads.reason: Local-only, largely requires a hostile local user or predictable temp-path condition, and is a weaker remote-security candidate than the decoder issues.

summary: Reviewed the Netty 4.1.71.Final-SNAPSHOT source snapshot with emphasis on remotely reachable decoders (HTTP/1.x, HTTP/2, HAProxy, DNS, MQTT, SPDY, TLS, multipart) and the native loader. The strongest source-backed issue is an uncontrolled-recursion path in HAProxy proxy-protocol v2 TLV parsing: an unauthenticated remote peer can cause a StackOverflowError by nesting PP2_TYPE_SSL TLVs inside a single bounded proxy-protocol header. Other plausible issues were identified as rejected/secondary leads because they are either conditional on deployment/configuration or are hardening gaps rather than clearly exploitable defects in this snapshot.
